title: Ship 0.1.3 with the evidence bar and transition rule

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited 4d7ed29 (release content) + b1cc3c5 (bookkeeping). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict.

REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE

Req 1 — MET. qa1.md step 4 states the demonstration standard (counterexample, reproduction, or command output; not a reading of the code alone) and cites sprint 1's path-encoding blocker with the re-derivation detail.

Req 1a — MET. The counterweight is in the same paragraph, not a separate section, and is bolded like the standard itself, so a skimming reader hits both. Reader test applied: someone who stops early still lands on "one confirmed defect is enough for a FAIL, and an accurate verdict is never held open waiting for evidence that cannot change it." The LiveQA stall is cited as the real precedent. CONDITIONAL is explicitly bound to the same rule.

Req 1b — MET. Explicit: "Authoring tests for your own findings is Dev Team's job, not yours; a demonstration can be a one-off repro script or command you throw away, it does not need to become part of the suite." Bounds it without weakening the standard.

Req 2 — MET. Rule is in CLAUDE.md immediately after the tree-hash section, credited to the external team, with the worked example. I verified the claim against the code rather than the sprint file's phrasing: sprint_lifecycle.py:478 does accept dev_agreed_done, and carries a comment saying it exists precisely so ship's tree-hash error is not a dead end. The documentation matches the mechanism.

Req 2a — MET, and strongly. "Read this as a constraint on how a precondition gets added, never as a reason not to add one... The rule is 'pair every gate with a recovery path,' not 'don't add gates.'" No reasonable agent comes away thinking gates are discouraged.

Req 3 — MET with one defect, see ISSUE 1 below. Convention is recorded with reasoning inline, and cmd_dev_done's real handling (sprint_lifecycle.py:513-522, state.get("qa1_audit_file_hash") plus the migration comment) is cited accurately.

Req 3a — MET. git diff 0fd7973..4d7ed29 -- scripts/ is empty. Did not re-run smoke_test.sh: with zero changes under scripts/ there is nothing for it to regress against, and the acceptance criterion is the diff, which I verified directly.

Req 4 — MET. package.json is 0.1.3; the diff to that file is exactly one line.

Req 5 — MET as written, with a finding the criterion did not anticipate, see ISSUE 2. I ran npm pack myself, extracted the tarball, and additionally installed it into a scratch directory. docs/sprints/ in both tarball and installed target contains only the seven .gitkeep placeholders. No registry.json, no state/*.json, no sprint markdown under any phase folder, no .claude/settings.local.json. Nothing sprint-related in the file list, so this is not the FAIL the criterion describes.

Req 6 — MET. 4d7ed29 touches exactly .claude/agents/qa1.md, CLAUDE.md, package.json (35 insertions, 2 deletions). Bookkeeping is correctly isolated in b1cc3c5. All four target commits confirmed ancestors of 4d7ed29 via git merge-base --is-ancestor: f2557d4 yes, 2238f44 yes, 192de1d yes, 0fd7973 yes.

ISSUE 1 — REQUIRED FIX (minor severity, but it is a defect in this sprint's own text)

CLAUDE.md, the new state-field access paragraph. The definition given is temporal and correct ("fields that have been in a sprint's state dict since it was first created"). The lookup shortcut offered in the parenthetical is not: "see cmd_start: id, phase, qa1_audit_result, audit_rounds, history, and the rest of that literal."

Demonstrated by reading cmd_start's literal at sprint_lifecycle.py:415-429. It contains fourteen keys today, and five of them are post-hoc additions: qa1_audit_file_hash, qa1_audited_tree_hash, last_shipped_commit, groundtruth_result, live_test_rounds. A reader who follows "the rest of that literal" indexes qa1_audit_file_hash directly and breaks cmd_dev_done's migration path.

That is not a hypothetical misread. It is the exact field the same paragraph holds up as the .get() precedent, so the paragraph's cited lookup method contradicts the paragraph's cited example. This is also precisely the failure Req 3a exists to prevent: someone "fixing" the .get() into direct indexing.

Fix is one line and touches no code. Either drop "and the rest of that literal", or qualify it: cmd_start's literal today also contains later additions like qa1_audit_file_hash, and the test is when a field was added, not whether it appears there now.

ISSUE 2 — NOT A FIX FOR THIS SPRINT. MASTER CONTROLLER SCOPE DECISION, NEEDED BEFORE PIPEMAN PUBLISHES.

Req 5a names the stake as this machine's home-directory paths and the real client project name "Licenseprofessor Edits and fixes", and calls it information disclosure. It assumes the only vector is the state files. It is not.

Demonstrated, not argued. I packed the real tarball, installed it into a clean scratch directory, and grepped the result:
  /tmp/fc-target/scripts/launcher/session.js:67 — "(`~/Programming/Licenseprofessor Edits and fixes`, seven such"
That is the client name plus the directory-count observation, verbatim, written into every installing project. scripts/launcher is FRAMEWORK_OWNED, so install.js copies it into every target and overwrites it on every upgrade. The tarball also carries scripts/launcher_test.js:128 with a hardcoded /Users/chrishobbs/... path.

This is the fail-open denylist Req 5 warns about, landing on a file nobody thought to look at. It is pre-existing, not introduced here: git log -S confirms it entered in 896cac3 (sprint 1's fix commit), so it already shipped in 0.1.2 and is already public. This release republishes it.

I am not making this a required fix, because fixing it inside this sprint would directly violate Req 3a's "git diff shows zero changes under scripts/" and Req 6's "nothing in scripts/ changes" — I would be demanding a change I then have to fail. The sprint file already says who owns that call: scope decisions are Master Controller's, not Dev Team's. It pairs naturally with the package.json files-allowlist item already deferred in Out of Scope.

Sequencing note: this CONDITIONAL returns the sprint to dev_build, which is a clean window for Master Controller to amend scope if it wants the comment rewritten. If the sprint file is amended, re-run /sprint-qa1 against the amended file — expected, not a bug.

ISSUE 3 — INFORMATIONAL, FOR PIPEMAN

npm pack packs the working tree, not the audited commit. .vscode/settings.json is currently modified and uncommitted (fullyCompletely.autoLaunch flipped false to true), and Out of Scope says leave it alone, so it will still be dirty at publish time. The packed tarball carries autoLaunch: true while the audited commit has false.

Verified inert this release: .vscode is not in FRAMEWORK_OWNED, and mergeSettings (install.js:311-327) hardcodes the value false and never reads the source file. Installing the tarball into a scratch target produced autoLaunch: false, as it should. So no action needed on this file — but the general gap is real. What ships is the working tree, and only the commit gets audited.

CODE QUALITY

Test coverage: none added, correctly. Documentation and a version string; Req 3a and Req 6 forbid touching scripts/. Existing suite is untouched and unaffected.
Error handling: n/a, no code paths changed.
Standards compliance: both CLAUDE.md additions are accurate against the code they describe. I re-derived both claims from the script rather than trusting the sprint file's phrasing, and both hold. Commit hygiene is right — content and bookkeeping split, which is what makes Req 6's check land cleanly.
Security: the tarball carries no sprint data. It does carry a client project name and a developer home path in source comments, see Issue 2.

RECOMMENDATION

Fix Issue 1 (one line in CLAUDE.md), re-run /sprint-qa1 3, then dev-done and ship. Master Controller should rule on Issue 2 before Pipeman publishes; if it amends the sprint file, that forces a re-audit, which is the check working as intended.

PASS: PASS — round 2. Audited 9938716 (fix) on top of 4d7ed29 (release content); HEAD is 89c8a74, bookkeeping only.

Sprint file re-read: verified byte-identical to b1cc3c5 by SHA-256 (d833cca5...aec7d, git blob vs working tree). No commit has touched it since it was moved into 2-in-progress, and it is unmodified in the working tree. Nothing was amended mid-build.

ROUND-1 CONDITIONAL: CLEARED

The state-access paragraph no longer points at cmd_start's literal as the base-schema list. It now gives the list explicitly (id, title, phase, qa1_audit_result, groundtruth_result, audit_rounds, live_test_rounds, started, completed, history) and adds a bolded caveat that this is NOT the same list as cmd_start's dict literal, naming the three post-hoc fields it also seeds (qa1_audit_file_hash, qa1_audited_tree_hash, last_shipped_commit) and stating they must stay .get()-only.

This is a stronger fix than deleting the shortcut would have been. The old text made a wrong inference available; the new text names that exact inference and forbids it — "don't take 'it's in cmd_start's literal' as license to index a field directly." The failure mode is now blocked by name, not just left un-suggested.

Verified against the code, not the commit message: cmd_start's current literal (sprint_lifecycle.py:415-429) holds thirteen keys, ten in the base list plus exactly the three named post-hoc fields. Arithmetic checks out.

REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE — ALL MET

Req 1 / 1a / 1b — unchanged since round 1, all met. Demonstration standard present with the sprint 1 citation; counterweight in the same paragraph and bolded, so an early-stopping reader still gets it; test-authoring bound explicit.
Req 2 / 2a — unchanged, met. Rule present with the tree-hash worked example, verified against sprint_lifecycle.py:478 and its comment. Framed as a constraint on how, not whether.
Req 3 — met, defect from round 1 fixed. Reasoning inline; cmd_dev_done's real .get() handling at 513-522 cited accurately.
Req 3a — met. git diff 0fd7973..HEAD -- scripts/ is empty. Did not re-run smoke_test.sh: with zero changes under scripts/ there is nothing to regress, and the criterion is the diff, which I checked directly.
Req 4 — met. 0.1.3, one-line diff, unchanged this round.
Req 5 — met. Re-ran npm pack after this round's CLAUDE.md change and re-extracted, because the content moved and a round-1 result would have been stale. Tarball's docs/sprints/ contains only the seven .gitkeep placeholders. No registry.json, no state/*.json, no sprint markdown, no .claude/settings.local.json. Packed version reads 0.1.3.
Req 6 — met. Cumulative content diff from 0fd7973 is confined to .claude/agents/qa1.md, CLAUDE.md, package.json; everything else in the range is docs/sprints bookkeeping in b1cc3c5 and 89c8a74. Four target commits re-confirmed as ancestors in round 1 and unchanged since.

STILL OPEN — MASTER CONTROLLER, BEFORE PIPEMAN PUBLISHES

Round 1's Issue 2 is unfixed and correctly so. scripts/launcher/session.js:67 ships the real client project name "Licenseprofessor Edits and fixes" and the directory-count observation into every installing project — scripts/launcher is FRAMEWORK_OWNED, so install.js writes it into the target and overwrites it on every upgrade. Demonstrated in round 1 by installing the actual tarball into a scratch directory. Pre-existing since 896cac3, already public in 0.1.2, so not a regression and not a blocker for this audit. But this release republishes it, and fixing it inside this sprint would violate Req 3a and Req 6. Master Controller's scope call. Pairs with the package.json files-allowlist item already deferred in Out of Scope.

INFORMATIONAL — NO ACTION THIS SPRINT

1. groundtruth_result and the base list. Strictly, that key was not present at the dict's first schema (798aaeb had qa_auto_live_result and qa1_final_result); it arrived as a rename at 236ba3a. The classification is nonetheless correct in practice and I am not holding the verdict on it: no state file predates the rename (sprints 1, 2 and 3 all carry the key), and the script already indexes it directly at lines 450 and 688. Recorded only so the next person re-deriving this list against 798aaeb doesn't spend an hour on the same discrepancy I did.

2. The convention has four pre-existing violations in the file it governs. state.get("history", []) at lines 459 and 898, state.get('audit_rounds', 0) and state.get('live_test_rounds', 0) at 981-982 — all four are base-list fields read with .get(). Not a defect in this sprint's text, which is explicitly forward-looking ("Follow this for the next field added to the schema"), and Req 3a forbids touching scripts/ anyway. Flagged because a future agent reading the new convention may decide to "fix" them, which is churn Req 3a exists to prevent. If anyone wants them aligned, that is its own sprint with its own audit.

3. For Pipeman, sequencing. The tree hash recorded by this PASS is HEAD's tree at 89c8a74. If the PASS bookkeeping is committed before shipping, HEAD moves and its tree no longer matches. Ship --commit 89c8a74 (or any commit preserving that exact tree), not the bookkeeping commit that lands after this verdict.

4. For Pipeman, carried from round 1. npm pack packs the working tree, not the audited commit, and .vscode/settings.json is still dirty (autoLaunch flipped to true) because Out of Scope says leave it alone. Verified inert: .vscode is not FRAMEWORK_OWNED and mergeSettings (install.js:311-327) hardcodes false and never reads the source file; a scratch install produced false. No action needed on the file — but what publishes is the working tree, and only the commit gets audited.

CODE QUALITY

Test coverage: none added, correctly — documentation and a version string, with Req 3a and Req 6 forbidding scripts/ changes.
Error handling: n/a, no code paths changed.
Standards compliance: both CLAUDE.md additions verified against the code they describe rather than against the sprint file's phrasing. Both hold. Commit hygiene right again — the fix is isolated from bookkeeping.
Security: tarball carries no sprint data. It does carry a client project name and a developer home path in source comments; see STILL OPEN.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. Run /sprint-dev-done 3, then hand 89c8a74 to Pipeman. Master Controller should rule on the session.js client-name disclosure before publish; if it amends the sprint file to bring that into scope, dev-done will refuse until this is re-audited, which is the check working.

PASS: PASS — round 1. Live-tested the published npm package 0.1.3, no browser (the package is the product, per the sprint file's redefinition block). Environment: macOS, npx against the real registry, two scratch directories (/tmp/fc-fresh, /tmp/fc-upgrade), 2026-08-29.

PROVENANCE CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY BEFORE TESTING
`npm view fully-completely version` -> 0.1.3; dist-tags latest -> 0.1.3; versions [0.1.0, 0.1.1, 0.1.2, 0.1.3]. Critically, `npm view fully-completely@0.1.3 gitHead` -> 89c8a74bff0ec64b529d45d5b1a49e23a9d730d0, an exact match for last_shipped_commit. So the artifact I tested is provably the commit QA1 audited, established from npm rather than accepted from a handoff.

CRITERION 1 — INSTALL FRESH: PASS
`npx -y fully-completely@0.1.3` in an empty /tmp/fc-fresh. Printed verbatim: "Fully Completely: installed into /private/tmp/fc-fresh" / "Installed 0.1.3 (first install)". Exit code 0. 44 files copied, marker file .claude/fully-completely-version reads 0.1.3. Asserted on the printed string as the criterion requires, not on the file — the marker is corroboration, not the check.

CRITERION 2 — REAL 0.1.2 -> 0.1.3 UPGRADE: PASS
This is the path with one prior live test that failed, so I ran it as a real before/after, not a smoke test.

Baseline: installed 0.1.2 into /tmp/fc-upgrade, marker read 0.1.2. Confirmed by grep that 0.1.2 contains ZERO occurrences of all four retro-edit strings (verified-how prompt, liveqa evidence bar, CLAUDE.md transition rule, qa1 demonstration standard). The release premise and the external team's report are both corroborated empirically, not assumed.

Then planted realistic downstream project data the upgrade must not destroy: docs/sprints/registry.json with two of ITS OWN sprints, docs/sprints/state/sprint-2.json, two sprint markdown files under 2-in-progress and 3-done, plus sentinel customisation lines appended to CLAUDE.md and .claude/agents/qa1.md.

Upgrade printed verbatim: "Upgraded 0.1.2 -> 0.1.3". Correct, and specifically NOT the class of lie sprint 2 caught. Marker moved to 0.1.3. Replaced exactly one framework file: "templates/sprint-template.md (upgraded, previous version backed up to templates/sprint-template.md.fc-bak-0.1.2)". Verified the backup exists (681 bytes) and holds the OLD content (0 occurrences of the verified-how prompt).

No corruption, no discard — every planted item verified intact by content after the upgrade: DOWNSTREAM-STATE-MUST-SURVIVE, SENTINEL-SPRINT-MD-MUST-SURVIVE, "Downstream project sprint two" in the registry, SENTINEL-CLAUDEMD-CUSTOMISATION-MUST-SURVIVE, SENTINEL-QA1-CUSTOMISATION-MUST-SURVIVE. All present. The target's own sprint numbering was untouched.

CRITERION 3 — RETRO EDITS ARRIVED: PASS
The load-bearing half, on the upgrade path: templates/sprint-template.md is FRAMEWORK_OWNED, and it genuinely upgraded. Occurrences of "verified how?" went 0 (0.1.2) -> 1 (after upgrade); "assert on the printed/displayed output itself" likewise present; file checksum changed 6f3c09b9... -> fcb802cb.... This is the entire point of the release and it demonstrably reached the target.

The .claude/agents/liveqa.md half was verified on the FRESH install, where the exact string "A PASS needs all the evidence; a FAIL or CONDITIONAL needs one" is present. See the ownership note below for why that is the correct place to score it.

CRITERION 4 — NEW RULES ARRIVED: PASS (scored on fresh install)
In /tmp/fc-fresh: CLAUDE.md contains both "Transition-precondition design rule" and "State-field access convention". .claude/agents/qa1.md line 34 carries the demonstration standard AND its counterweight together — "demonstrated, not argued", "counterexample", and "one confirmed defect is enough" all on the same line, which also satisfies Req 1a's same-paragraph requirement as a shipped fact rather than a source-tree fact.

OWNERSHIP NOTE, VERIFIED IN CODE NOT ACCEPTED ON ASSERTION: install.js declares USER_OWNED = ['.claude/agents', 'CLAUDE.md', 'docs/sprints'] and FRAMEWORK_OWNED includes templates/sprint-template.md. I read those lists and the two install loops in the source myself before scoring. Consequence: CLAUDE.md and every agent file are never overwritten on upgrade — they are reported as conflicts. So criterion 4, and the liveqa.md half of criterion 3, are only scoreable on a fresh install. Testing them against an upgrade would be reporting documented installer behaviour as a defect, and I did not. The upgrade target correctly still shows 0 occurrences of all three of those strings, with all seven user-owned files listed under "Conflicts — left untouched, review by hand".

CRITERION 5 — NO SPRINT DATA IN TARGET: PASS
Fresh target's docs/sprints/ contains exactly seven .gitkeep placeholders and nothing else (0 non-.gitkeep files). A find across the whole target for registry.json, sprint-N.json, sprint-N.md and settings.local.json returned nothing. Confirmed independently of QA1's tarball check, as the criterion requires. The upgrade target likewise received no leak — none of this repo's sprint titles appear anywhere under its docs/.

TRIED TO BREAK IT
Re-ran the installer on both already-current targets. Both printed "Already at 0.1.3 (re-run, nothing to upgrade)" with no Replaced and no Removed section beneath it — the message is truthful, which is exactly the failure mode install.js's own comments record QA1 and LiveQA catching one round apart. Conflicts persist correctly across re-runs. Idempotent.

ISSUES — NONE BLOCKING, THREE FOR THE RECORD

1. MEDIUM, NOT MINE TO GATE — the client name is live in the published artifact. /tmp/fc-fresh/scripts/launcher/session.js:67 contains verbatim: "// (`~/Programming/Licenseprofessor Edits and fixes`, seven such". QA1 demonstrated this in round 1 from a locally-packed tarball; I am confirming it from the REAL published npm package, and I confirmed it is present in published 0.1.2 as well, so QA1's "already public" call is correct. scripts/launcher is FRAMEWORK_OWNED, so this is written into every installing target and overwritten there on every upgrade. It is outside all five of my acceptance criteria (criterion 5 is scoped to docs/sprints content, which is clean) and QA1 correctly ruled fixing it here would violate Req 3a and Req 6. Not grounds to fail this release. Recorded because it has now shipped in a second published version and remains an open Master Controller scope call. One narrowing datapoint: no "/Users/chrishobbs" string appears anywhere in the installed target — QA1's launcher_test.js:128 concern does not reach an installing project, since that file is not FRAMEWORK_OWNED.

2. LOW, INFORMATIONAL — a successful upgrade exits 1. Because all six agent files plus CLAUDE.md are user-owned and upstream changed them, every 0.1.2 -> 0.1.3 upgrade produces seven conflicts, and conflicts set process.exitCode = 1. The upgrade genuinely succeeded and the accompanying message is accurate and helpful, so this is documented behaviour and not a defect. Flagged only because any CI or scripted install that checks exit status will read a fully successful upgrade as a failure.

3. LOW, INFORMATIONAL — the sprint file's "four unpublished commits" is imprecise, and this is the assumption its own External dependency flagged as unverified from inside the repo. npm reports 0.1.2's gitHead as 2238f44158b25b3b5e1e9908ec19b066f0e00d09, meaning 0.1.2 was published from a tree that already contained f2557d4 and 2238f44. So two of the four "never published" commits were in fact already in the 0.1.2 tarball. The consequential half of the claim holds and I verified it directly rather than inferring it: 0.1.2 contains zero occurrences of all four retro-edit strings, so 192de1d and 0fd7973 genuinely never shipped and the release premise is sound. No effect on this verdict.

WHAT I OBSERVED VS ACCEPTED
Everything above I ran and observed directly on macOS against the live npm registry. Nothing in this verdict is accepted on report from another role. No Windows component in this sprint's criteria, so unlike sprint 1 there is no user-executed part to fold in.

RECOMMENDATION
Ship-ready. All five LiveQA criteria pass with evidence. The release does what it exists to do — the verified-how prompt provably reaches an upgrading target, which is the gap that made this sprint necessary. Master Controller still owns the session.js client-name call before the next publish; sprint 4 already covers scrubbing the shipped client name, which is the right home for it. This PASS means the code is ready, not that anyone is authorized to close sprint 3.
